title: How to turn your AI into a world-class designer
note: Anshu Chimala guest post in Lenny’s Newsletter, Sep 2026. Primary source for techniques 1–8.
coverage: Free preview covers Discover + Define through technique 6 (cut elements) with worked examples (productivity landings, critic loops, image/video, calorie-tracker cuts). Technique 7 (Remove AI tells) and 8 (hand-rewrite copy) are named at the paywall boundary—deeper verbatim tips are paid. This catalog paraphrases Deliver-stage practice honestly and does not invent paywalled quotes.

title: Anshu Chimala on Substack
coverage: Cited for identity only. We do not invent or summarize unpublished Substack posts.

title: Sakana AI — String Seed of Thought
note: Sakana AI — String Seed of Thought (SSoT). Cited by Anshu as inspiration for seed-string variety injection; also useful as distribution-faithful diversity prompting. No endorsement.
coverage: Method reference (https://sakana.ai/ssot/); not a full technique reprint. Anshu’s catalog adaptation uses external shell entropy rather than in-model string generation.

title: design-slop-cop
note: Adrian Krebs — independent public tooling for spotting design slop. Cited alongside remove-ai-tells / Build Games anti-slop practice; not a full designer entry (tooling depth only). No endorsement.

title: How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it to explore ideas before building them
note: Nate Parrott (Anthropic). Public source for the eleven partial-catalog techniques.
coverage: Full public post: best-practice list (thinking before prompt through keep working alongside) plus Make it alive craft notes and product examples (intro animation editor, subway physics, color sliders). No endorsement.

title: Cooking with constraints: A designer’s framework for better AI prompts
note: Greg Huntoon, Figma Blog (Jan 2026). Public source for TC-EBC. Earlier catalog stub mis-attributed this lineage to David Kossnick—corrected.
coverage: Full public post: mise en place framing; TC-EBC definitions; pantry-app and feature-copy before/after; revision + model-choice notes. Catalogued as five partial techniques (Task…Constraints). No endorsement.

title: TC-EBC Prompt Framework (reference repo)
note: Canonical short-form TC-EBC skeleton by Greg Huntoon.
coverage: Format reference for prompt skeletons used in this catalog.

title: Transitions.dev — free UI transitions for agents
note: Jakub Antalik. Free copy-paste transition recipes used for Quiet Folio motion (texts-reveal, number-pop-in, tabs-sliding, restrained card-tilt, success-check, skeleton-reveal). No Pro recipes.
coverage: Cited as product motion craft (free recipes) for Quiet Folio chrome. Adapted to ink craft tokens; prefers-reduced-motion honored. No endorsement.

title: Bret Victor — Stop Drawing Dead Fish
note: Public talk cited by Nate Parrott as the north star for “make it alive”: everything we draw should be alive by default. No endorsement.
coverage: Talk citation only — used on make-it-alive; not a full technique catalog.

title: Designing Depth — Rauno Freiberg
note: Rauno Freiberg (July 2024). Public craft essay on layered composition, blurred backdrops, motion choreography and stagger. Source for designing-depth and stagger-choreograph-motion. No endorsement.
coverage: Full public essay paraphrased into procedures/prompts; no paywalled material.

title: Great Animations — Emil Kowalski
note: Public principles: natural, fast, purposeful, performant, interruptible, accessible, cohesive. Source for purposeful-motion. No endorsement.
coverage: Public web essays paraphrased; animations.dev course content not used.

title: You Don't Need Animations — Emil Kowalski
note: Public essay on purpose, frequency, and when no animation is best. Source for animation-restraint. No endorsement.
coverage: Public web essays paraphrased; animations.dev course content not used.

title: A Brief History & Ethos of the Digital Garden — Maggie Appleton
note: Public essay on garden patterns including imperfection/status disclosure. Source for garden-status-labels. No endorsement.

title: How to Draw Invisible Programming Concepts: Part I — Maggie Appleton
note: Public essay on source→target metaphors for abstract concepts. Source for illustrate-the-invisible. No endorsement.
coverage: Full public essay paraphrased; illustrations not copied.

title: 7 Practical Tips for Cheating at Design — Refactoring UI
note: Public Medium tip list (Wathan/Schoger). Source for hierarchy-with-weight, start-with-whitespace, fewer-borders. No endorsement; paid book not quoted.

title: Refactoring UI — public site / previews
note: Marketing site and free previews (e.g. color palette). Cited for public tip lineage. No endorsement.

title: What Screens Want — Frank Chimero
note: Frank Chimero (2013). Public essay: screens’ grain is flux. Source for screens-want-honesty. No endorsement.

title: The Web’s Grain — Frank Chimero
note: Companion to What Screens Want; web-native humility. Cited on screens-want-honesty. No endorsement.
